newsitem.title: CHINA: China couple abandons seven daughters in son quest.
newsitem.headline: China couple abandons seven daughters in son quest.

text.p: A Chinese villager and his wife who had 11 daughters in a fruitless quest for a son have been found guilty of abandoning seven of the girls, the Books and Newspapers Digest said.

A court in Lianyuan city in central Hubei province earlier this year sentenced Liu Junxing, 40, to two and one half years in prison for abandoning seven daughters between 1973 and 1993, the newspaper said in an edition seen in Beijing on Saturday.
Liu's wife Liu Huixiang was sentenced to two and a half years in prison but the sentence was suspended for three years, meaning she might not go to jail at all.
The couple's desperation for a son forced them to move home frequently in an attempt to avoid being fined for breaking China's population laws, the newspaper said.

After the birth of their 11th daughter in June 1993, the couple abandoned the infant in a pile of straw outside a house, the newspaper said without giving details of the fate of any of the couple's other children.

China officially limits families to one child but the rule is less strictly enforced in the countryside where officials often turn a blind eye to a second or third if there is no son to help with farm work.
China's population control laws prompt some families to abandon -- or even kill -- unwanted daughters, researchers say.
The traditional desire for a son to continue the patriarchial family line is particularly strong in rural areas.
